stories.headline: India’s tea output drops 10% in July to 164 m kgs on heavy rains, floods
stories.title: India’s tea output drops 10% in July to 164 m kgs on heavy rains, floods
stories.summary: In Assam, the largest producing state, output dropped 13% to 91.08 m kg during July 2026 over corresponding last year’s 105 m kg, as per the Tea Board’s latest data
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India’s July tea output drops by a tenth to 164 m kgs on excess rains and floods impacting output in top two producing sates of Assam and West Bengal, while production registered a growth of around 18 per cent in South India.
In Assam, the largest producing state, output dropped 13 per cent to 91.08 m kg during July 2026 over corresponding last year’s 105 m kg, as per the Tea Board’s latest data.

In the Assam Valley region, the production was down 12.7 per cent at 86.96 m kg over previous July’s 99.66 m kg, whereas in Cachar the decline was about 23 per cent at 4.12 m kg (5.34 m kg in July 2025).
Parts of Assam and North Bengal had witnessed heavy rains triggering floods during July.
In neighbouring West Bengal, tea production declined 14 per cent to 43.87 m kg (50.96 m kg).
In Dooars region the output declined 13 per cent at 24.83 m kg (28.51 m kg), while in Terai the production dropped 15 per cent at 18.23 m kg (21.50 m kg).
Also in Darjeeling the output declined 15 per cent at 0.81 m kg (0.95 m kg) impacted by heavy rains.
The other tea producing states in North India saw an output decline by 16 per cent at 4.82 m kg (5.73 m kg).
However, in South India, the production improved across al three states.

In Tamil Nadu, tea output during July was up 22 per cent at 19.45 m kg (15.92 m kg), while in Kerala, it was up marginally at 4.70 m kg (4.64 m kg) and in Karnataka by 41 per cent at 0.41 m kg (0.29 m kg).
Across the country, CTC tea production stood at 143.10 m kg during July, while orthodox tea output was 18.76 m kg.
Green tea production in the country stood at 2.47 m kg.

stories.headline: CM’s helpline emerges as lifeline for residents outside UT
stories.title: CM’s helpline emerges as lifeline for residents outside UT
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 1: A toll-free helpline launched by the Omar Abdullah-led government in the aftermath of the Pahalgam terror attack has evolved into a round-the-clock support mechanism for residents of Jammu and Kashmir facing difficulties across India and abroad. The 24x7 helpline (1800-8900-166) was launched on April 25, 2025, to assist students and residents of J&K following reports of intimidation, harassment and assaults on people from the Union Territory studying or working outside. Set up through the Chief Minister’s Office, the helpline was initially intended to provide emergency assistance, coordinate with state governments and law-enforcement agencies, and offer families a direct channel to seek help. Officials said the service has since expanded into a single-window support platform, assisting students, facilitating emergency travel, coordinating with local administrations and addressing various public-service-related concerns. One of its significant interventions came during the Iran-Israel conflict, when students from Jammu and Kashmir were stranded amid escalating tensions. The helpline helped maintain communication with affected students, their families and authorities while facilitating the flow of information during the crisis. The service also received appreciation from students and families following the Pahalgam attack, when uncertainty and concerns over the safety of J&K residents outside the UT were high. Officials said the helpline has handled thousands of calls and messages despite being managed by a single officer posted at the Chief Minister’s Secretariat. The officer monitors calls, coordinates responses and follows up with departments and authorities across jurisdictions. Government sources said the initiative reflects the administration’s effort to remain accessible beyond conventional office channels and provide residents with direct access to government assistance regardless of their location. More than a year after its launch, the helpline has increasingly become a support and reassurance mechanism for students, workers, professionals and families from Jammu and Kashmir seeking assistance away from home.

stories.title: Dr. Farooq calls for end to Middle East conflict
stories.summary: Srinagar, Sep 1: Jammu and Kashmir National Conference president Dr Farooq Abdullah on Tuesday expressed concern over the continuing conflict in the Middle East and its widening humanitarian and economic consequences. Abdullah appealed to countries, world leaders and the United Nations to take urgent and meaningful steps to end the ongoing war and restore peace and stability in the region. He said prolonged conflicts not only cause immense human suffering but also have serious repercussions for the global economy, aggravating poverty and hardship worldwide. Abdullah also called for an immediate end to the Israel-Palestine conflict and urged all sides to work towards a peaceful and lasting resolution.

stories.headline: The bonds yield warning markets can no longer ignore
stories.title: The bonds yield warning markets can no longer ignore
stories.summary: Global bond yields seem to be in a relentless race to the top. As yields across long-tenured securities hit fresh highs, they are creating an additional hurdle for emerging markets like India. Higher returns on US Treasuries make safe-haven assets more attractive for investors. The shift can moderate foreign portfolio inflows (FPIs), put additional pressure on stock valuations and dampen risk appetite, particularly in sectors that depend on abundant liquidity and low interest rates.“Global bond yields remain an important headwind for emerging-market equities. Higher US yields reduce the relative attractiveness of emerging-market equities and can delay the return of large foreign flows into India,” says Uttam Srimal, deputy research head, Axis Securities.Fresh escalation in the West Asia crisis lifted oil prices above $90 a barrel as investors grew worried about inflationary risks putting pressure on bond markets, indicating a rise of capital costs. The 10-year US Treasury yield, hit its highest since early 2025 at 4.78 percent on August 31; Japan's 10-year benchmark hit 3 percent for the first time, while futures for French and German debt extended selling earlier drove yields to 15-year highs.“The way yields are rising everywhere tells you the market is now firmly pricing a US Federal Reserve rate hike this year; the odds of a September hike, which looked increasingly unlikely barely a week ago, have jumped to almost two-thirds after Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish Jackson Hole speech, and by December a hike is priced as close to certain,” says Shrikant Chouhan, head equity research, Kotak Securities. In his debut speech on August 29 at the central bank's annual Jackson Hole economic conference, US Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh maintained a hawkish commentary with focus on price stability and emphasised on the strength in the economy.“The recent selloff in long-dated US Treasuries is notable because it has occurred even after the Federal Reserve stopped shrinking its balance sheet,” says Sneha Pandey, fund manager-fixed income, Quantum AM. “This suggests that the market's attention is gradually shifting from monetary policy towards fiscal dynamics. Investors are increasingly focussed on the volume of debt that the US Treasury must issue and whether demand can keep pace with that supply,” she adds.Also Read: It is time for interest rates to go upMeanwhile, US national debt passed the $40-trillion mark in August, partly due to rise in treasury yields. The debt rise came after the US Treasury announced more than doubling the maximum debt buyback for longer-dated securities (10-30 years) to at least $4 billion per operation. While US national debt is 126 percent compared with the size of the economy, it's lower than other G7 nations Japan and Italy.“It is obvious that the action is an attempt to cool the sharp rise in long-term bond yields, such as the 30-year bond yield. A sharper rise in long-term bond yields relative to short-term bonds since 2023 has resulted in the normalisation of the yield curve, which had inverted during 2022-24. This has multiple implications for global capital markets, including Indian equities,” says Vinod Karki, equity strategist, ICICI Securities. He adds that concerns regarding rising US debt levels are resulting in dollar alternatives like gold and bitcoin rising while the dollar index weakens.What about foreign capital?Yields of Indian bond have been volatile due to factors like global policy uncertainty, weak Indian rupee, pressure on domestic liquidity and impact of the West Asia crisis. However, coordinated monetary and fiscal policy response have supported yields broadly. The gap between India and US 10-year yield is at a multi-year low and far below long-run average, which may have further aggravated the FPI-debt outflow.According to Karki of ICICI Securities, steepening of the US yield curve increases risk-free rate for US investors, which means they may dump riskier assets like emerging markets equities. “Rising long-term bond yields in the US is likely to raise the hurdle rate for investing in emerging markets and could limit FPI equity flows, unlike the earlier environment of low US interest rates,” he says. However, he argues that if growth in corporate continues to pick up in India going forward, FPI flows are likely to continue despite higher yields.Nearly half of FPIs in Indian stocks come from the US, which accounts for 44 percent of asset under management (AUM) from FPIs worth nearly Rs 31 trillion. In the last few months, foreign institutional investors (FIIs) have been significantly selling off Indian stocks while foreign direct investments (FDI) have also thinned out. However, towards the end of Q1FY27, FPI equity outflows began to recede, and inflows began to trickle in. Simultaneously, FDI and FPI-debt inflows improved meaningfully to $7.8 billion and $5.7 billion for Q1FY27.Meanwhile, India’s Minister of Finance Nirmala Sitharaman said India is on track to bring its government debt down to 50 percent of GDP by 2030. While addressing the Indian diaspora in Chicago on August 29, she emphasised that fiscal consolidation will continue without compromising spending on social welfare.

stories.headline: Delhi Cabinet clears free rooftop solar systems for households using up to 400 units
stories.title: Delhi Cabinet clears free rooftop solar systems for households using up to 400 units
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Delhi Cabinet on Tuesday approved second amendment to Delhi Solar Energy Policy, 2023, under which rooftop solar systems of up to 3 kW will be installed for free for domestic consumers with an average consumption of up to 400 units per month.

Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said consumers using up to 200 units of electricity would not only continue to receive the subsidy after installing rooftop solar systems but would also earn an energy-saving incentive for the electricity they save.
The government has set a target of installing solar systems on 2.3 lakh rooftops and adding 500 MW of rooftop solar capacity by March 2027.
Ms. Gupta said work to install solar systems on government buildings is already under way.
In addition to the ₹78,000 subsidy provided by the Central government, the Delhi government will provide a Capital subsidy of ₹78,000.
It will also provide an additional top-up to cover the difference between the subsidies and the tendered cost of the solar plant, the Chief Minister’s Office stated.
Power Minister Ashish Sood said the government has “shattered the AAP’s (Aam Aadmi Party) massive lie that free electricity cannot be sustained”.
“We have not only kept free electricity alive, but have secured and institutionalised it for the next 25 years,” Mr. Sood said.

stories.headline: Supreme Court to hear bail plea of Bhima Koregaon accused Surendra Gadling on October 14
stories.title: Supreme Court to hear bail plea of Bhima Koregaon accused Surendra Gadling on October 14
stories.summary: The present bail plea arises from the 2016 Surjagarh arson case, in which several vehicles transporting iron ore from Surjagarh mines in Maharashtra’s Gadchiroli district were allegedly set ablaze by persons associated with the banned Communist Party of India (Maoist)
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court said on Tuesday (September 1, 2026) that it would hear on October 14 a bail plea filed by advocate and activist Surendra Gadling in connection with the 2016 Surjagarh iron ore mine arson case.
Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Mr. Gadling, told a Bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Augustine George Masih, and Sandeep Mehta that his client had been incarcerated for over seven years.
He pointed out that Mr. Gadling was also an accused in the Elgar Parishad-Maoist links case and had already been granted bail in that case.
“Another case was foisted on him at the same time,” Mr. Sibal submitted.
Additional Solicitor General S.V. Raju, appearing for the Maharashtra government, urged the Bench to list the matter on a non-miscellaneous day to allow for a detailed hearing.
“I have to point out the evidence against him,” Mr. Raju said.

The present bail plea arises from the 2016 Surjagarh arson case, in which several vehicles transporting iron ore from Surjagarh mines in Maharashtra’s Gadchiroli district were allegedly set ablaze by persons associated with the banned Communist Party of India (Maoist).
Mr. Gadling has been lodged in Taloja Central Prison since June 2018, following his arrest in the Elgar Parishad-Maoist links case.
The prosecution alleges that provocative speeches delivered at the Elgar Parishad conclave in Pune on December 31, 2017, triggered violence near the Koregaon-Bhima war memorial the following day.
He was subsequently arrested in February 2019 in connection with the Surjagarh arson case.

On January 31, 2023, the Nagpur Bench of the Bombay High Court rejected his bail plea, observing that the allegations concerning his membership of the banned Maoist organisation appeared prima facie true.
He subsequently approached the Supreme Court, which issued a notice on his petition on October 10, 2023.

stories.title: Supreme Court Quashes FIRs Across Country Over Student Protests; Bars Future FIRs
stories.summary: The Court said the order is passed keeping in mind the students' future.

event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Court said the order is passed keeping in mind the students' future.

The Supreme Court today ordered that the FIRs registered across the country, in any State or Union Territory, over the student protests held between July 20 to July 25, should not be pursued or investigated and must be treated as closed for all intents and purposes.
The Court also quashed the FIRs over student protests which were specified in the applications filed by the Centre (Delhi.
Police), Bihar, West Bengal, Maharashtra and Assam.
Though only the Centre and the above-said four states filed the applications seeking to quash the FIRs, the Court extended the application of the order pan-India.
The Court said that it was passing the order considering the future of the students who bona fide came to the protests.
The Court also ordered that no state/UT shall register any fresh FIR in relation to protest incidents between July 20-25.
The Court has however allowed the Delhi.
Police to pursue one FIR against 2,873 individuals who were present in the Jantar Mantar protests as they had serious criminal antecedents.
The bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana passed the directions invoking the Court's special powers under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.
The bench clarified that the order has been passed in view of the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, and shall not be treated as a precedent.

The bench recorded the Solicitor General's statement that a policy for grant of compensation to the families of students who died by suicide following the NEET-UG 2026 cancellation will be formulated within three months.
